record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.original_question: Is the countable power of the Niemytzki plane homogeneous?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Is the ωth power of the Niemytzki plane homogeneous?
Observe that the Niemytzki plane is not metrizable. This problem is open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}$ denote the Niemytzki plane (Moore plane): the set $L = \{(x,y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : y \geq 0\}$ equipped with the topology generated as follows. For a point $p = (x,y)$ with $y>0$, basic neighborhoods of $p$ are ordinary open Euclidean disks centered at $p$ that lie entirely in the open upper half-plane. For a point $p = (x,0)$ on the $x$-axis, basic neighborhoods of $p$ consist of $\{p\}$ together with an open Euclidean disk in the upper half-plane that is tangent to the $x$-axis at $p$.

A topological space $X$ is called homogeneous if for any two points $a, b \in X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h : X \to X$ with $h(a) = b$.

Let $\mathbb{N}^\omega$ denote the countable infinite Cartesian power of $\mathbb{N}$ equipped with the product topology.

Question: Is $\mathbb{N}^\omega$ homogeneous?
artifact.status_search_result: The original problem list explicitly states this problem is open, and a web search did not turn up any subsequent resolution. The Niemytzki plane is a well-known non-metrizable Tychonoff space, and no reference to a proof or disproof of homogeneity of its countable power was found.

status_evidence.title: Moore plane - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Moore plane (Niemytzki plane) is a completely regular Hausdorff space that is not normal; it is first countable but not second countable or Lindelöf.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference confirms properties of the Niemytzki plane; no mention of resolution of homogeneity of its countable power.

status_evidence.title: On some modifications of the Niemytzki plane
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on modifications of the Niemytzki plane.
status_evidence.claim: Recent activity around the Niemytzki plane exists but does not resolve the homogeneity of its countable power.
